title: Ingest heuristics, regression checks, and publish flow for tuned and quantized model onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
Add a robust ingest and publish workflow for newly onboarded tuned and quantized model variants that: 1) automatically enriches manifests with inferred runtime constraints and quantization metadata, 2) runs deterministic regression checks against perf and quality baselines, and 3) publishes a curated performance profile + pin only after passing gating checks. This ticket covers implementation of heuristics used during ingest, automated regression tests, integration with the pin/publish pipeline, and the docs/playbook update for SREs/PMs/designers to follow during release.

Scope and goals:
- Heuristics: derive recommended memory/sequence capacity, preferred kernel family, and quantization profile tags from manifest + artifact heuristics (file sizes, dtype signatures, layer counts).
- Regression checks: run a lightweight synthetic perf suite (latency P50/P95, throughput at sample QPS) and a quality smoke harness (acceptance prompts + embedding similarity / response-stability) with thresholds defined per-model-family.
- Publish flow: only allow pinning to stable if: ingest heuristics populate required fields, regression checks pass, and an automated review note is created. Provide canary publish mode with 1% traffic routing for 24h.
- Docs: update onboarding playbook, manifest schema examples (tuned/quantized), and a new checklist for Solutions/SEs.

Decisions & trade-offs so far:
- Chose to run lightweight synthetic perf (microbench) during ingest instead of full benchmarking to keep ingest latency under 10 minutes for hosted ingestion. Full benchmarking remains a separate opt-in job. Trade-off: less exhaustive perf data at publish time, compensated by canary window + monitoring.
- Quantization metadata will be inferred and stored as "quant_profile:v1" tags instead of trying to canonicalize across vendors initially. This decreases upfront complexity but requires future harmonization work.
- Regression thresholds are conservative (lenient on latency increases for small models, strict for production-grade LLMs) to reduce false rejects on early onboarding.

Progress updates (chronological):
- 2025-02-18: RFC drafted and shared with model-onboarding WG (link below). Initial heuristic list and schema additions proposed.
- 2025-02-21: Spike completed to extract dtype/param-count/shape signatures from PyTorch/ONNX tarball samples. Prototype script: tools/ingest/heuristics/extract_signature.py (internal repo).
- 2025-02-25: Regression harness implemented (microbench) and integrated into ingest pipeline via ephemeral dedicated runner. Baseline metrics collection using synthetic prompts added.
- 2025-02-27: First end-to-end test with a locally tuned llama forked variant passed heuristic enrichment but failed the quality smoke test (response stability < threshold). Logged follow-up to adjust threshold and add more representative prompts (ENG-19735).
- 2025-03-01: Design/PM review: agreed on canary window of 24h and 1% traffic, requirement for an automated publish note and explicit human approval only when canary shows anomalies.
- 2025-03-03: QA approved ingest heuristics; integrating pin gating into publish pipeline. Draft docs for onboarding checklist created (confluence link).

Open tasks and next steps:
- Integrate canary routing with Smart Routing service (work queued with ENG-18099).
- Add vendor-normalization pass for quant_profile tags (follow-up spike).
- Write the acceptance test suite and add a post-publish monitoring dashboard tile.
- Update SDK docs with new model metadata fields (owner: SDK).

Acceptance criteria:
- Manifest enrichment runs for new ingestions and fills required fields for runtime, quant_profile, and estimated KV size.
- Ingested model must pass regression harness thresholds to be eligible for pin publishing, otherwise it enters a review queue.
- Publish pipeline prevents pin until gating checks succeed or explicit human override recorded.
- Playbook and onboarding checklist published in Confluence; internal training session scheduled.

Rollout plan:
1) Roll out heuristics + regression harness to internal staged ingest (no public catalog publish). 2) Enable canary publish for internal partners (SEs). 3) Open to public catalog with canary enforced for 24h and monitoring.

Artifacts & links:
- RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/MC/ingest-heuristics-rfc
- Playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/MC/onboard-playbook-draft
- Prototype script (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/tree/main/tools/ingest/heuristics
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/982 (regression harness), https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1007 (manifest enrichment)
updates: 2025-02-21: Prototype extractor committed; initial tests on LLama variants show consistent dtype signatures.
2025-02-25: Microbench regression harness merged to staging; runtime env containerization passes security scan.
2025-02-27: Quality smoke test failure logged; PM requested wider prompt set to reduce false positives.
2025-03-01: Canaries and gating policy approved in review meeting; Diego to coordinate Smart Routing integration.
2025-03-03: QA sign-off on heuristics; started wiring publish gate.
acceptance_tests: On ingest, manifest contains fields: recommended_max_seq, kv_estimate_bytes, quant_profile, kernel_hint
Model that passes harness can be pinned via automated flow and create publish note
Model failing harness is flagged and routed to review queue; override requires audit note
notes_for_docs: Add examples for quant_profile tags and how they map to runtime flags
Document canary behavior and how to monitor canary metrics in Console
Include troubleshooting section for common failure reasons from regression harness
